81.t:
There is disagreement about his name:
The people of Medina say: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays ibn Zāʾidah ibn al-Aṣamm ibn Rawāḥah al-Qurashī, al-ʿĀmirī.
As for the people of Iraq: they called him ʿAmr.
His mother was Umm Maktūm: she is ʿĀtikah bint ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAnkathah ibn ʿĀmir ibn Makhzūm ibn Yaqaẓah al-Makhzūmiyyah.
He was among the earliest emigrants.
He was blind, and was a muezzin for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ together with Bilāl, Saʿd al-Qaraẓ, and Abū Maḥdhūrah, ⟦1:360⟧ the muezzin of Mecca.
He emigrated a short time after the battle of Badr.
Ibn Saʿd said this.
The Prophet ﷺ used to hold him in respect, and would appoint him as his deputy over Medina, and he would lead the remaining people in prayer.
al-Shaʿbī said: The Prophet ﷺ appointed ʿAmr ibn Umm Maktūm as deputy, to lead the people in prayer, and he was blind (1), and that was during the expedition of Tabūk, so he said.
But what is preserved is that the Prophet ﷺ only appointed over Medina at that time: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (2).
Qatādah said: The Prophet ﷺ appointed Ibn Umm Maktūm as deputy over Medina twice, and he was blind (3).
وروى: مجالد (4) ، عن الشعبي:
That the Prophet ﷺ appointed Ibn Umm Maktūm as deputy over Medina at the battle of Badr (5), and this invalidates what has preceded.
It is also invalidated by the hadith of Abū Isḥāq, from al-Barāʾ, who said:
The first to come to us was Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr, then after him ʿAmr ibn Umm Maktūm came to us.
They said to him: What has happened to those you left behind?
He said: They are right behind me (6).
شعبة: عن أبي إسحاق، سمع البراء يقول:
The first to come to us were Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr and Ibn Umm Maktūm, and they began teaching the people the Qurʾān (7). ⟦1:361⟧
حماد بن سلمة: حدثنا أبو ظلال، قال:
I was with Anas, and he said: When did you lose your eyesight?
I said: When I was small.
He said: Gabriel came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while Ibn Umm Maktūm was with him, and said: (When did you lose your sight?).
He said: When I was a boy.
He said: Allah the Exalted said: (When I take away the dearest thing of My servant, I find no reward for him except Paradise (1)).
ʿĀʾishah said: Ibn Umm Maktūm was a muezzin for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was blind (2).
وروى: حجاج بن أرطاة، عن شيخ، عن بعض مؤذني رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال:
Bilāl would give the call to prayer and Ibn Umm Maktūm would give the second call, and sometimes Ibn Umm Maktūm would give the call and Bilāl would give the second call (3).
Its chain of transmission (إسناد) is feeble.
Ibn ʿUmar said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Bilāl gives the call to prayer at night, so eat and drink until Ibn Umm Maktūm calls).
He was blind, and would not call until it was said to him: You have reached dawn, you have reached dawn (4).
ʿUrwah said: The Prophet ﷺ was with some men of Quraysh, among them ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah, and Ibn Umm Maktūm came asking about something, but he turned away from him.
So there was revealed: “He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him” (Qurʾān 80:1-2) ⟦1:362⟧ (1).
al-Wāqidī: حدثني عبيد الله بن نوح، عن محمد بن سهل بن أبي حثمة، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed Ibn Umm Maktūm as deputy over Medina, and he would lead them in the Friday prayer and deliver the sermon beside the pulpit, placing it on his left (2).
يونس بن أبي إسحاق: عن أبيه، عن عبد الله بن معقل، قال:
Ibn Umm Maktūm stayed with a Jewish woman in Medina who used to be kind to him but would insult the Prophet ﷺ in his presence, so he took hold of her, struck her, and killed her.
The matter was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he himself said:
By Allah, she was indeed kind to me, but she harmed me regarding Allah and His Messenger.
The Prophet ﷺ said: (May Allah remove her far away; I have annulled her blood-money (3)).
أبو إسحاق: عن البراء، قال:
When there was revealed: “Not equal are those who sit” (Qurʾān 4:95), the Prophet ﷺ called Zayd and instructed him, and he came with a shoulder blade and wrote it down.
Then Ibn Umm Maktūm came and complained of his blindness, and there was revealed: “other than those who have a disability” (Qurʾān 4:95) (4). ⟦1:363⟧
ثابت البناني: عن ابن أبي ليلى:
That Ibn Umm Maktūm said: O Lord! Reveal my excuse.
So there was revealed: “other than those who have a disability”.
After that he used to go out on campaigns, and would say: Hand the banner to me, for I am blind and cannot flee, and station me between the two ranks (1).
عبد الرحمن بن أبي الزناد: عن أبيه، عن خارجة بن زيد، عن أبيه، قال:
I was beside the Prophet ﷺ when tranquillity enveloped him, and his thigh fell upon my thigh, and I never felt anything heavier than it; then it lifted from him.
He said to me: (Write).
So I wrote on a shoulder blade: “Not equal are those who sit among the believers and those who strive” (Qurʾān 4:95).
Then ʿAmr ibn Umm Maktūm stood and said: What of one who is unable?
His words had not yet ended when tranquillity enveloped the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then it lifted from him.
He said: (Write: “other than those who have a disability” ).
Zayd said: Allah revealed it on its own, and it is as though I am looking at its place of attachment at the crack in the shoulder blade (2).
ابن أبي عروبة: عن قتادة، عن أنس:
That ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm had a black banner with him on the day of al-Qādisiyyah, and he was wearing a coat of mail of his (3). ⟦1:364⟧
أبو هلال: عن قتادة، عن أنس:
That ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zāʾidah, who is Ibn Umm Maktūm, was fighting on the day of al-Qādisiyyah, wearing a strong, full coat of mail of his (1).
al-Wāqidī said: He took part in al-Qādisiyyah carrying the banner, then returned to Medina and died there, and we have not heard any mention of him after ʿUmar.
I say: It is said that he was martyred on the day of al-Qādisiyyah.
Narrating from him: عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى (a mursal (مرسل) report), وأبو رزين الأسدي, and others.
Al-Qādisiyyah was a great battle (2), which took place in Iraq, with Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ over the Muslims, and over the polytheists Rustam, Dhū al-Ḥājib, and al-Jālīnūs.
Abū Wāʾil said: The Muslims were more than seven thousand, and the enemy was forty thousand.
It is also said: sixty thousand, with seventy elephants among them.
al-Madāʾinī said: They fought for three days, at the end of Shawwāl in the year 15 AH, and Rustam was killed and they were routed. ⟦1:365⟧
